# Verification record 2026-10-11

<!-- Generated by `node design/compatibility/verification.mjs render` from 2026-10-11.json; do not edit. -->

**Verification is evidence, not a support guarantee.** This record is the result of one full nightly run of the [compatibility matrix](../cells/COMPATIBILITY.md) at commit `10cd4a46ab1f2b36c54e75129efc6c048c14d19e`, with each render backend checked separately. The machine-readable record is [2026-10-11.json](2026-10-11.json); `verifiedRanges` in [seed.json](../seed.json) is derived from the records (`node design/compatibility/verification.mjs ranges`), and `validate.mjs` checks that they agree.

**Rendering: software (GPU profile `software`).** Software rendering: no GPU took part. WebGL ran on ANGLE over SwiftShader and WebGPU on Dawn over SwiftShader's Vulkan device, a fallback adapter (isFallbackAdapter true). It counts as verification; a run on a real GPU (run-cells.mjs --gpu hardware) can be added later as extra evidence.

Rule: A tuple (React adapter, exact React, Pixi adapter, exact pixi.js) is verified on a render backend when its cell passed on that backend in this record (every command, every conformance scenario and the render check) and every boundary probe and every negative case of this record behaved as expected. A backend run that applied an environment shim (adapterMatrix.environmentShims, a labelled workaround for an upstream pixi.js bug) is judged like any other: a pass verifies the tuple, which carries the shim id, and a failure is a failure. A run a record before 2026-10-11 lists as an expected blank render (the retired expectedBlankRender list) verifies nothing. Each tuple lists every backend it is verified on; backends are never inferred from each other.

## Run

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build --force`
- `node design/compatibility/cells/run-cells.mjs pack --out <work>/tarballs`
- `node design/compatibility/cells/run-cells.mjs run --tier nightly --patches all --cell <a third of the cells> --no-cache --work <work> --tarballs <work>/tarballs   (three shards in parallel)`
- `node design/compatibility/cells/run-cells.mjs probes --tier nightly --work <work>`
- `node design/compatibility/cells/run-cells.mjs run --negative --no-cache --work <work> --tarballs <work>/tarballs`
- `node design/compatibility/cells/run-cells.mjs data --work <work> --tarballs <work>/tarballs`
- `node design/compatibility/verification.mjs build --work <work> --date 2026-10-11 --commit 10cd4a46ab1f2b36c54e75129efc6c048c14d19e --extra <notes>`

- Tier: nightly with `--patches all` (297 cells: every React adapter, React 18.0 to 19.3, at its minimum and latest audited patch x the newest audited patch of every Pixi 8 minor and pixi.js 7.2.0, 7.2.4, 7.3.0, 7.3.3, 7.4.2 and 7.4.3), a superset of the scheduled nightly tier's 216 cells. Render backends: WebGL and WebGPU; Pixi 7 cells WebGL only.
- First record with environment shims (adapterMatrix.environmentShims, owner ruling 2026-10-11): every WebGPU run of the pixi-8 adapter with pixi.js >=8.2.6 <8.10.0 (88 runs: 8.2.6, 8.3.4, 8.4.1, 8.5.2, 8.6.6, 8.7.3, 8.8.1 and 8.9.2 x 11 React versions) applied pixi-webgpu-texture-units, which clamps WebGL MAX_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS to 16 before Pixi initializes; each reported 32 -> 16. No WebGL run and no run on pixi.js 8.10+ applied it.
- Same machine and software profile as the 2026-10-10 records, which it supersedes (only the newest record of a machine and GPU profile counts). Those ran without the shim and keep their 64 and 88 WebGPU expected blank renders on 8.2-8.9 as recorded.
- Commit 10cd4a4 on claude/webgpu-texture-units-shim, run from a separate worktree of that commit. Fresh: a new work directory, packages rebuilt with `pnpm build --force`, tarballs packed from that build, `--no-cache` (no verdict reused), CI=true. The npm download cache was shared (registry tarballs are integrity-checked).
- Three cell shards (every third cell each) ran in parallel on 4 vCPUs with the probes (cells 02:18 to 03:04 UTC, 46 minutes), then the negative cases and the data-only probes. No test timed out and no failure was retried.
- Cells with React 18.0.0, 18.1.0 and 18.2.0 ran with harness/test/lend-act.ts; Pixi 7.2 cells compiled the Pixi 7 type consumer without the pixi8-names-rejected assertions (typeAssertions, from 7.3.0), as in 2026-10-10.2.
- Commits after this one change documentation, generated tables, the verification tooling and tests only; `node design/compatibility/verification.mjs compare --record 2026-10-11 --tarballs <fresh pack>` shows whether a later commit packs the same code (Markdown and build logs aside).

## Environment shims and known issues

\* WebGPU on pixi.js <8.10 needs the workaround for [pixijs/pixijs#11389](https://github.com/pixijs/pixijs/issues/11389) (fixed in 8.10.0): without it, WebGPU renders a blank canvas on devices whose WebGL texture-unit count exceeds their WebGPU per-stage limit. Use pixi.js 8.10+ or WebGL. The verification runs apply that workaround as the labelled environment shim `pixi-webgpu-texture-units` (`adapterMatrix.environmentShims`). This record verified 88 WebGPU tuples it covers (pixi.js 8.2.6, 8.3.4, 8.4.1, 8.5.2, 8.6.6, 8.7.3, 8.8.1, 8.9.2), marked in the cells table; they stay verified (owner rulings 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-11).

- Environment shim `pixi-webgpu-texture-units` (WebGPU): applied to 88 runs on pixi.js 8.2.6, 8.3.4, 8.4.1, 8.5.2, 8.6.6, 8.7.3, 8.8.1, 8.9.2, 88 passed; MAX_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS 32 → 16. Marked "(shimmed)" in the cells table.

## Cells

Each backend column shows the status and the conformance scenarios passed/skipped/failed (skips are scenarios whose capability the cell does not provide). Each backend run also has a render check (harness/test/backend.test.tsx: the requested renderer is the one Pixi created, and a screenshot of the canvas shows the red rectangle it drew); "render check FAIL" marks a run whose scenarios passed but whose canvas stayed blank. "(shimmed)" marks a run that applied an environment shim, and a footnote mark a verified tuple a known issue covers (see above). Pixi 7 has no WebGPU renderer (n/a).

## Findings

- WebGL: all 297 cells passed (every command, every conformance scenario, the render check).
- WebGPU: all 231 Pixi 8 cells passed and are verified on WebGPU, every React adapter and patch on every Pixi 8 minor. The 88 runs on pixi.js 8.2.6 to 8.9.2 applied the environment shim pixi-webgpu-texture-units (WebGL MAX_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS 32 clamped to 16) and rendered the red rectangle; in 2026-10-10.2, without the shim, the same 88 runs showed a blank canvas. They carry the footnote: WebGPU on pixi.js <8.10 needs the workaround for pixijs/pixijs#11389 (fixed in 8.10.0); without it, WebGPU renders a blank canvas on devices whose WebGL texture-unit count exceeds their WebGPU per-stage limit. Use pixi.js 8.10+ or WebGL.
- The shim changes nothing in the adapters or the checks: every conformance scenario ran as written, and the WebGL runs and the pixi.js 8.10.2 to 8.22.0 WebGPU runs, which apply no shim, passed as in 2026-10-10.2.
- Rendering was software throughout (no GPU in the machine): WebGL on ANGLE/SwiftShader, WebGPU on SwiftShader's fallback adapter. Owner ruling: software rendering counts as verification; the Apple M5 Max hardware record adds real-GPU evidence (its WebGL reports 16 texture units, so the shim changes nothing there: hardware record 2026-10-11-macos-26-apple-m5-max (Node 22.22.0, superseding 2026-10-10-macos-26-apple-m5-max) logged the shim's original value as 16 (16 → 16 on all 88 shimmed runs); the owner's Windows PC, an NVIDIA RTX 4070 on ANGLE over Direct3D 11, also reported 16 in a standalone probe, not yet a record).
- Boundary probes: 51 of 51 passed (pixi-8.5.0 by failing exactly as the audit recorded). Incompatible pairs: 7 of 7 rejected as expected.

## Data only, not verified

**Data only, not verified: these results are never verification, never enter verifiedRanges and never change a peer range.**

Data-only probes (issue 17). Each probe installs the packed adapters beside a React or pixi.js the adapter does not declare, ignoring peers, and records what every cell command does. The adapters' environment checks are bypassed in the conformance run only (cell.json dataOnly.bypassEnvironmentCheck), so the suite shows what would happen past them. Results are data, never verification: nothing here enters verifiedRanges or changes a peer range.

### pixi7-earlier-releases

The Pixi 7 adapter on pixi.js releases outside its peer range: the highest patch of 7.0 and 7.1 (below the 7.2.0 floor), and the excluded 7.4.0 (7.4.1 was never published to npm). Pixi 7.2 and 7.3, and React 18.0 to 18.2, were data-only probes until they became matrix cells (React 18 per-minor packages, the Pixi 7 range widened to 7.2).

- pixi.js 7.4.1: not run, absent from the npm registry's version list and time map: there is nothing to install.

### Data-only findings

- pixi.js 7.4.0: the adapter's entry fails to import in plain Node ('Worker is not defined', a pixi.js 7.4.0 module-scope dependency on a browser global); in Chromium, past checkEnvironment(), the whole suite passes with React 18.3.1 and 19.3.0; types pass. It stays excluded from the peer range.
- pixi.js 7.1.4 and 7.0.5: the adapter cannot load. pixi.js 7.1 does not export HTMLText, and 7.0 does not export the filters or HTMLText from its root, which the adapter's entry imports by name: Node import and the browser build fail, so no conformance scenario ran. Types also fail.
- pixi.js 7.4.1 was never published to npm, so nothing ran for it.
